## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library("tidyverse")
library("here")
```

## Load dataset

```{r}
ab_bind = read_csv(here('data/01_dat_load_experimental.csv')) |>
  select(
    pdb = `#PDB`,
    partners = `Partners(A_B)`,
    mutation = Mutation,
    ddg = `ddG(kcal/mol)`,
    pdb_ph = `PDB pH`,
    assay_name = `Assay Name`,
    assay_ph = `Assay pH`
  )


ab_bind
```

## Drop rows with multiple mutations, insertions or deletions
In our analysis we will focus on single point mutations for the sake of simplicity.
Point mutations always consist of 
1) a single chain letter
2) a comma separator
3) a single-letter uppercase amino acid code
4) one or more digits specifying the position
5) a single-letter uppercase amino acid code
which can be matched with a simple regex:

```{r}
ab_bind <- ab_bind |>
  filter(str_detect(mutation, "^[A-Za-z]:[A-Z][0-9]+[A-Z]$"))

ab_bind
```


## Drop rows that are not antibody-antigen

In the paper they note that chains of antibody-antigen systems were named with
'H' for the heavy chain and 'L' for the light chain. We therefore assume that any
PDB with 'H' and 'L' as chain names is antibody-antigen. For the remaining
PDBs, we manually review them.
```{r}
pdb_partners <- ab_bind |>
  distinct(pdb, partners)

pdb_hl <- pdb_partners |>
  filter(str_detect(partners, "H"), str_detect(partners, "L"))

pdb_no_hl <- pdb_partners |>
  anti_join(pdb_hl, by = "pdb")

pdb_no_hl
```
After manually visiting these PDB entries on https://rcsb.org we find that the following do not contain antibody-antigen structures:
- 1AK4
- 1FFW
- 1JTG
- 1KTZ
- 3K2M
- HM_1KTZ

These PDBs contain only constant regions of antibodies which do not contain the CDR regions that form the typical binding interface of an antibody, so we also exclude these:

These PDBs contain antibodies, but the binding interface is at the Fc region and not at the CDR region which is the region that determines antigen binding:
- 1T83
- 3WJJ

This leaves us with two PDBs: 3NPS and 1DVF which both contain canonical antibody-antigen complexes

PDB 3NPS:
heavy: chain B
light: chain C
antigen: chain A

Note that PDB 1DVF contains an _antiidiotopic_ antibody, which means it's an antibody that binds to another antibody.
For this structure, we both add a row where antibody 1 is the antibody and antibody 2 is treated as the antigen and vice versa.
In this one, chain C and D are one antibody and chain A and B are one antibody
heavy 1: chain B
light 1: chain A
heavy 2: chain D
light 2: chain C

```{r}
ab_bind_hl <- ab_bind |>
  filter(pdb %in% pull(pdb_hl, pdb)) |>
  mutate(heavy = 'H', light = 'L')

ab_bind_3nps <- ab_bind |>
  filter(pdb == "3NPS") |>
  mutate(heavy = 'B', light = 'C')

ab_bind_1dvf_1 <- ab_bind |>
  filter(pdb == "1DVF") |>
  mutate(heavy = 'B', light = 'A')

ab_bind_1dvf_2 <- ab_bind |>
  filter(pdb == "1DVF") |>
  mutate(heavy = 'D', light = 'C')

ab_bind_ab <- bind_rows(
  ab_bind_hl,
  ab_bind_3nps,
  ab_bind_1dvf_1,
  ab_bind_1dvf_2
)
ab_bind_ab
```

## Rename light and heavy chains
```{r}
ab_bind_ab <- ab_bind_ab |>
  mutate(
    mutation = str_replace_all(mutation, str_c("(^|,)", heavy, ":"), "\\1H:"),
    mutation = str_replace_all(mutation, str_c("(^|,)", light, ":"), "\\1L:"),
    partners = str_replace_all(partners, heavy, "H"),
    partners = str_replace_all(partners, light, "L"),
    partners = str_replace_all(partners, "LH", "HL"),
    antigen_chains = str_remove(partners, "HL_|_HL")
  ) |>
  select(!c(heavy, light, partners))

ab_bind_ab
```

## Join with computational data
Some of the computational methods have duplicate predictions, so we take the mean in those cases
```{r}
comp <- read_csv(
  here("data", "01_dat_load_computational.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(pdb %in% pull(ab_bind_ab, pdb)) |>
  mutate(
    method = case_when(
      method == "bASA_all_side" ~ "basa_all_side",
      method == "d_studio_expt_comp" ~ "d_studio",
      method == "dDfire" ~ "ddfire",
      method == "dfire" ~ "dfire",
      method == "foldX_IE" ~ "foldx",
      method == "rosetta_expt_comp" ~ "rosetta",
      method == "statium_expt_comp" ~ "statium"
    )
  ) |>
  summarise(comp = mean(comp), .by = c(method, pdb, mutation)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = comp) |>
  rename(
    d_studio_ddg = d_studio,
    ddfire_ddg = ddfire,
    dfire_ddg = dfire,
    foldx_ddg = foldx,
    rosetta_ddg = rosetta,
    statium_ddg = statium
  )

ab_bind_ab <- ab_bind_ab |>
  left_join(comp, by = c("pdb", "mutation"))

ab_bind_ab
```

## Split mutations into columns
```{r}
ab_bind_ab <- ab_bind_ab |>
  mutate(
    mut_chain = str_sub(mutation, 1, 1),
    mut_position = str_sub(mutation, 4, -2),
    mut_from = str_sub(mutation, 3, 3),
    mut_to = str_sub(mutation, -1, -1)
  ) |>
  select(-mutation)

ab_bind_ab
```

## Reorder columns
```{r}
ab_bind_ab <- ab_bind_ab |>
  select(
    pdb,
    starts_with("mut_"),
    ddg,
    ends_with("_ddg"),
    basa_all_side,
    assay_ph,
    pdb_ph,
    everything(),
  )

ab_bind_ab
```
## Write cleaned csv
```{r}
write_csv(
  x = ab_bind_ab,
  file = here("data", "02_dat_clean.csv")
)
```
